title: Existence of the Goldreich–Levin output
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a Boolean function, and let $\tau\in\mathbb{Q}$ satisfy $0<\tau\le 1$. For each coordinate set $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and each $S\subseteq J$, suppose a rational estimate differs by less than $\tau^2/4$ from the sum of squared Fourier coefficients of $f$ over all sets of the form $S\cup T$, where $T\subseteq J^c$. Then the Goldreich–Levin procedure with threshold $\tau$ and these estimates returns a finite family of coordinate sets.
hypotheses_covered: For every $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and $S\subseteq J$, the rational estimate differs from the restricted Fourier weight by less than $\tau^2/4$
